Senses.Explanation: Walking on ice is an exposed, precarious advance where a careless step cannot be recovered. Chan masters pair it with walking a sword blade to criticize timidity, describe the stakes of life and death, or show that even an apparently flawless course remains hazardous. Xieyunji pairs living together with walking on ice and a sword blade before asking about living together without dying together. Shengke Deyu calls Qianfeng's refusal to raise a second point overly timid, like walking on ice and a blade. Huitang Zuxin compares faultless movement that does not disturb grass or water to riding a horse across ice, still short of the archer's hand. Zhangxue Tongzui uses the same ice-and-blade pair in a direct hall sermon on entering an assembly. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

How would you get here? — and for the cold-ash bean-burst arrival: just look where the melting happens, Shiqi Tongyun writes the mourning layman: know where the love-thought arises and that very thought melts — the buddhas' wondrous meanings and the hundred thousand gates melt with it, and the standing place melts of itself, Yingshan Zhiyin's hesitation essay walks the midway road — fire-pit ahead, wolves and tigers behind, knives on the left and thorns on the right — till, like Lingyun at the peach blossoms, the doubt-mass breaks and no karma-delusion stays unmelted, this time reaching the ground of no doubt, and Jieweizhou Xingzhou opens and closes the retreat: at the binding the six senses are tied into one bundle and thrown into the great furnace, forged morning and evening till the ice melts and the tiles crumble; at the loosening the eighty-four thousand pores spring open, lights and wonders raining their flowers. Fangrong Ruxi judges the birthday scene — one cry at birth: heaven above, heaven below, I alone am honored; six snow-mountain years melted like ice; all beings hold the thus-come's wisdom — and rules that neither reading has scratched the sage's itch, Yunsou Benzhu stages the founder on the whisk-tip pointing sky and earth, struck by Yunmen's sudden blow: the earth and mountains melt, the myriad forms' eyes spring open — and he re-issues the order himself, and Huigong Kaixiong comments on the Dongyuan record: a pinch on the knee or a roar of laughter, and the order would have melted at once — even the Shouchang master's last word, doting father that he was, but love not noticing its own ugliness.

Senses.Note: A warm breeze comes from the south and a faint coolness reaches the palace corner. The sensory line became a Chan reply associated with awakening to what is already present. Fushi voices it after a warning about receiving a donor’s food, Tianyin gives it after asking what can be discussed when words fail, Daxiu uses it to answer why the way directly before us is hard to see, and Hefeng closes an address on what does not need arrangement with it. Senses.Explanation: “A warm breeze comes from the south; a faint coolness stirs at the palace corner” makes a small felt change answer a large question. Fushi closes a donor-food warning with it; Tianyin gives it where argument has run out. Senses.Note: Yuanwu gives the pair as an answer to where the Buddhas emerge; later records connect hearing it with Dahui's awakening. Occurrences.Kwic: 不墜。大眾！既是師承不立，為什麼却代代相承？良久，云：葉零零兮秋暮半凋，花片片兮春暖齊發。次日上堂，僧問：如何是龍門境？師云：到者方知。如何是境中人？師云：兩脚蹈地。僧云：人境已蒙師指示，向上宗乘事若何？師云：誰知遠煙浪，別有好思量。僧云：恁麼則朝看雲冉冉，暮聽水潺潺。師云：禮拜著。乃云：見聞不脫，如水中月，每日山色水聲、名花異鳥、滿眼滿耳，作麼生說得箇脫底道理？要會麼？暢暢，釋迦老子無伎倆；休休，龍門山水天下幽。夜來一覺到天明，得風流處

Senses.Note: The pair is dismissive, but the surrounding passages determine what is being dismissed. Shitian explicitly tests the stance with the demand for the meals; Xuefeng combines it with a second, steadier image.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，舉：一拳拳倒黃鶴樓，一趯趯翻鸚鵡洲。有意氣時添意氣，不風流處也風流。俊哉俊哉，快活快活，一似十七八歲少年作狀元相似。誰管你天，誰管你地。心王不妄動，六國一時通。罷拈三尺劒，休弄一張弓。自在自在，快活快活，恰似七八十老人作宰相相似。風以時，雨以時。五穀植，萬民安。乃竪起拄杖，云：大眾！這兩箇并山僧拄杖子，共作得一箇。衲僧到雪峯門下，但知隨例飡䭔子，也得三文買草鞋。喝一喝，卓拄杖，下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1346.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xuefeng Huikong. Xuefeng Huikong speaks in his own address, which opens by raising the couplet about smashing Yellow Crane Tower and overturning Parrot Islet. The headword means: Who cares about your heaven? Who cares about your earth? The pair follows the image of the seventeen- or eighteen-year-old examination champion. It precedes the unmoving mind-king, sheathed weapons and old-minister image. His staff gesture combines these rather than declaring the first image sufficient by itself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 歲夜。烏兔東西疾，一秊時序畢。竇八布衫穿，烏龜眼睛赤。肇法師剛道：物不迁，擔片板。見一邊，衲僧家。誰管你天？誰管你地？喫飯救飢，開口取氣。今年也如是，來秊也如是，後秊也如是，更後秊也如是，直得阿逸多出世也只如是。是則是，忽若閻羅老子徵飯錢，又却如何抵擬？普化出僧堂，波斯入閙市。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1386.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shitian Faxun. Shitian Faxun gives his own year-end instruction. The headword means: Who cares about your heaven? Who cares about your earth? After the pair come eating to stop hunger and opening the mouth to breathe, this year and year after year. Then comes the challenge about Yama collecting the cost of the meals. That challenge prevents the dismissive stance from being read as the last word.

Occurrences.Kwic: 送智維那往江西智不到處道一句，生鐵稱錘被蟲蛀。南北東西參學人，莫教踏著無生路。無生路上荊棘多，將心覔佛還成魔。閑伸兩脚睡一覺，任他日月如飛梭。誰管你天，誰管你地。說妙談玄，弄粥飯氣。馬祖出八十四人，問著無有不會。直饒歸宗較些子，也是瞎驢趂大隊。如今好箇太平時，佛法兩字誰論之。堂前青草深一丈，往往口角生膠黐。拈却德山棒，不用臨濟喝。寒則普天普地寒，熱則普天普地熱。要行便行歇便歇，切忌逡巡守途轍。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. Chushi Fanqi writes in his own authorial voice in the farewell verse for Zhi the precentor; this is not Guquan speaking his separate poem. The headword means: Who cares about your heaven? Who cares about your earth? Before it, he stretches his legs to sleep and lets the sun and moon hurry on. After it, he calls talk of mystery the energy of gruel and rice, and later urges going or resting without hesitation in established ruts. The local dismissal targets that verbal business, rather than explaining a theory about the heavens.

Senses.Explanation: Who cares about your heaven? Who cares about your earth? Xuefeng Huikong opens with smashing Yellow Crane Tower and overturning Parrot Islet, then compares the exuberance to a seventeen- or eighteen-year-old examination champion. The questions about heaven and earth belong to that energetic picture. He next gives a different picture: the mind's king does not move, the six states communicate, weapons are put away, and an old minister enjoys timely weather and an orderly realm. Raising his staff, he says that these two together with the staff make one. The pair therefore marks one side of an address that deliberately brings two kinds of bearing together. Shitian Faxun uses the pair in a year-end instruction. After calling a one-sided appeal to 'things do not move' a board carried on one shoulder, he gives the Chan monk's ordinary acts: eat to relieve hunger and open the mouth to breathe, this year and year after year. The dismissive questions fit that refusal to be occupied with the turning years. But he immediately asks how the assembly would answer if Yama demanded payment for the meals. His follow-up tests the stance he has just described rather than letting a carefree slogan finish the matter. Chushi Fanqi writes the pair in a farewell verse for Zhi the precentor, who is going to Jiangxi. He warns that searching for Buddha with the mind can turn into another obstruction, stretches out his legs for sleep, and lets the sun and moon hurry on. After the pair, he mocks talk of mystery as merely expending the energy of gruel and rice. The verse later tells the traveler to go when going and rest when resting, without hesitating in inherited ruts. The questions about heaven and earth help dismiss that busy explanatory talk; they are not an isolated cosmological proposition.
